# The Challenge — Hack the Lease

- **Host:** Hackberry Lane (operator of Haven on Geddes, Ann Arbor)
- **Ask:** Build a *working technical tool* that helps students choose housing based on **how they actually live** — schedule, budget, roommates, habits — **not demographics**.
- **Deadline:** Fri Nov 20, 5:00 PM (moved up from 6 PM), Ross R0230
- **Format:** 5 min demo + 5 min Q&A

## Judging rubric
| Weight | Criterion |
|---|---|
| 35% | It works (functioning, technical tool) |
| 30% | Problem framing & product choices |
| 20% | Decision quality, evidence & assumptions |
| 15% | UX |

## Hard requirements
- Demo must show **decision sensitivity**: change one input live → the recommendation changes.
- Any synthetic data (listings, student profiles) must be **clearly labeled as synthetic** on screen.

## Judges worth designing for
- Reid Marks — operates leases (cares about real leasing pain)
- Asher Lin — background in AI agents that flag issues in documents

# Product — what we're building

> Shared spec. Edit freely; the prompt rebuilds automatically on push.

## One-liner
A housing matcher that learns what a student *actually* values from a few quick trade-off choices, then ranks Ann Arbor apartments and explains why.

## Onboarding flow (target: ~5 clicks)
1. **Where's your week?** Central / North / Medical / Split / + work spot
2. **People + budget per person** (chips + slider)
3–4. **Two adaptive trade-off cards** (bisection on value of time vs. rent, e.g. "$200/mo cheaper but +20 min walk/day?")
5. **Dealbreakers** grid with must / nice toggles (in-unit laundry, AC, pets; parking only if they drive)
- Auto: lease = Fall 2027, 12 months (editable)
- Confidence meter: "We're 92% sure about your top 3 — refine?"

## Engine
- Weighted score per listing from learned weights (rent, commute time, amenities, dealbreakers).
- Next question = the one that best splits remaining synthetic profiles' top picks (ID3-style). Stop at ~90% agreement.
- Every recommendation shows a plain-English "why" (e.g. "You value your time at ~$18/hr, so B is worth the extra rent").

## Demo script (sensitivity)
Switch classes from mostly Central → mostly North; the #1 apartment flips live.

## Stretch
- Roommate mode: combine weights, show who compromises most, suggest fair rent split.

# In-app AI advisor (used by the website)

You are the housing advisor inside our Hack the Lease web app. You help University of Michigan students choose an Ann Arbor apartment based on how they actually live (schedule, budget, roommates, habits), never on demographics.

Rules:
- Ground every recommendation in the student's own inputs and the listing data you are given. Never invent listings, prices or commute times.
- Always explain *why* in one or two plain sentences, naming the trade-off (e.g. "B costs $90/mo more but saves you ~40 min of walking a week").
- If the listing data is synthetic, say so.
- Keep answers short and friendly; students are skimming on their phones.
- If an input is missing and it would change the top pick, ask for it in one question.
